extracted.intended_audience: DoD contracting officers, installation commanders, program managers, and policy/contracting analysts
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and evaluative standards for conducting OMB A-76 competitive sourcing studies, preparing key acquisition documents (PWS, QASP, Management Plan/MEO), performing cost comparisons, and addressing legal/organizational impediments. Focused on producing defensible solicitations and in-house estimates for DoD competitive sourcing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Performance Work Statement (PWS) - purpose and orientation
rubrics_metrics.description: The PWS defines what is being requested, the performance standards and measures and timeframes of performance.  The PWS is performance-oriented, stating what outputs or measures are desired as well as limiting directions, yet does not indicate to the supplier how a service should be accomplished.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Develop the PWS to ensure it does not limit service operations, arbitrarily increase risk, reduce competition, violate industry/service norms, or omit statutory or regulatory requirements. It must state outputs/measures/timeframes but avoid specifying methods ('how') so suppliers can propose solutions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quality Assurance Surveillance Plan (QASP) - role and content
rubrics_metrics.description: The QASP is designed to complement the PWS in that it describes the methods of inspections to be used, the reports required and the resources to be expended.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: QASP need not be published in the solicitation nor provided to Government employees developing the management study; competing sources are expected to develop a Quality Assurance Plan based solely on the PWS. Use QASP to translate PWS performance standards into inspection methods and reporting requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Management Plan / Most Efficient Organization (MEO) documentation
rubrics_metrics.description: The Management Plan detailing the Government's Most Efficient Organization (MEO) is the basis for the Government's in-house cost estimate and should reflect the scope of the PWS and identify the organizational structure needed to meet the outlined requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Management Plan should document best structure, staffing, operating procedures, equipment, inspection plans, assumptions used in developing the MEO and in‑house cost estimate (including organizational assets), and include the Quality Assurance Plan and Transition Plan. Use it as the in-house implementation blueprint and cost basis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Solicitation compliance and form (IFB/RFP) requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Solicitations must be issued in accordance with the FAR, Service regulations and any other applicable statutory requirements. Depending on the nature of the services, either an Invitation For Bid (IFB) or a Request For Proposal (RFP) can be used.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure the solicitation follows applicable procurement regulations and treats proposals with equal security protections. Choose IFB vs RFP consistent with procurement strategy and requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cost comparison procedure and responsiveness/responsibility evaluation
rubrics_metrics.description: Compare the in-house bid and the proposed contract or ISSA price. In sealed bids open all bids (including in-house estimate), enter prices on the cost comparison form, and announce a tentative decision subject to evaluation for responsiveness and responsibility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For negotiated/best value procurements, compare the most advantageous private sector or ISSA proposal against the in-house estimate on the Cost Comparison Form and award as required. Record comparisons formally and evaluate bidder responsiveness/responsibility before final award.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protest resolution as an inevitable final step
rubrics_metrics.description: The final step in the cost comparison process is the resolution of any protests by unsuccessful offerors, whether private sector, ISSA or in‑house organizations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognize protests as an inherent risk of promoting free and open competition; there are no guaranteed steps to eliminate them. Prepare robust documentation and defensible decision rationale to withstand protests.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expectation of savings and role of competition
rubrics_metrics.description: Competition is the key to successful application of A-76. Prior DoD A-76 competitions have shown associated cost savings (examples: 27%–36% in historical data).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not assume universal savings; treat competition as the mechanism to achieve efficiency, and if MEO wins it must perform at stated capability and within budget to retain credibility and avoid re-sourcing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reliability of projected savings and contributing risk factors
rubrics_metrics.description: GAO reported that neither DoD nor OMB has reliable data to assess the accuracy of savings estimates and identified contributing factors that may diminish projected savings, including mandated wage increases and poorly written PWS.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be cautious with savings projections. Use conservative assumptions, document data sources, and account for wage changes and the quality/completeness of the PWS when estimating expected savings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contractor 'low-balling' and post-award PWS deficiencies risk
rubrics_metrics.description: Contractor 'low-balling' during bidding and the revelation of PWS deficiencies after contractor operations can require contract modifications and price adjustments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Anticipate and mitigate low-balling by thorough PWS development, realistic cost estimates, and robust evaluation criteria; include mechanisms for handling discovered deficiencies without compromising value or fairness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition and classification of inherently Governmental vs commercial activities
rubrics_metrics.description: There is no consensus across Services on what constitutes a commercial activity or an inherently Governmental function; OMB A-76 lists numerous functions and Appendix B provides a comprehensive list of eligible commercial activities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain and update clear lists of commercial activities (per FAIR Act requirements) and consider consolidating lists across commands; document rationale for classification decisions to ensure consistency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Study timeframes and feasibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Single activity studies must be completed within 18 months, multi-service studies within 36 months; historically studies averaged 4 years 3 months (FY1987–1990).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognize shortened timeframes as ambitious; plan resources realistically, track milestones, and adjust scope if timelines are infeasible. Document schedule risks and contingency plans.

rubrics_metrics.name: Personnel availability and use of contractors for study work
rubrics_metrics.description: Downsizing has reduced personnel familiar with the A-76 process; Services have considered outsourcing parts of the A-76 study while retaining in-house cost estimate work and inherently Governmental functions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When outsourcing parts of the study, retain core inherently Governmental activities and in-house cost estimating to preserve accountability and defensibility; ensure contractors do not perform prohibited functions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Employee participation disincentives and legal restrictions
rubrics_metrics.description: Civil service employees may be reluctant to participate in PWS development due to fears of job loss or legal restrictions preventing displaced employees from working for the winning contractor for two years if they participated as a 'procurement official'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Anticipate low volunteer rates; communicate protections, clarify roles, and structure participation to avoid creating procurement official conflicts. Provide training and incentives where lawful and appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Commanders' control concerns and institutional knowledge loss
rubrics_metrics.description: Base commanders may fear losing control over performance of commercial services; relatively short tours of duty limit institutional knowledge and focus on short-term projects rather than long-term operational changes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Address command-level concerns by clarifying PWS scope, governance mechanisms, and performance oversight; capture institutional knowledge and include transition and oversight provisions in Management Plan and contracts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cost-comparison award threshold and best-value tradeoffs
rubrics_metrics.description: For a commercial activity to be awarded to a contractor, a contractor bid must meet a savings threshold of 10 percent of personnel costs or $10 million over the performance period. If threshold not met, activity remains in-house. In best-value procurements, trade-offs between contractor and Government proposals are evaluated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply the threshold consistently. Where best-value trade-offs are used, document rationale and allow MEO to modify operations to meet performance criteria before re-comparing costs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standardization (or lack) of Government operating cost measurement
rubrics_metrics.description: Supplement to OMB A-76 provides some guidance but is often silent on calculating some costs; there is no standard currently used to measure Government operating costs. DoD has looked to implement Activity Based Costing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adopt reproducible costing methods (e.g., Activity Based Costing) where possible, document chosen methodology, and acknowledge limits/assumptions. Strive for consistency across commands to improve comparability.

rubrics_metrics.name: PWS as the basis for cost capture and risks of incompleteness
rubrics_metrics.description: The PWS defines what costs must be captured and included in the competitive proposal submitted by the MEO; a critical factor is the completeness of the PWS in its ability to capture all of the work the Government expects to be performed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure PWS comprehensively captures tasks, locations, units, quantities, quality, and timeliness to avoid hidden costs and contract price increases. Validate PWS coverage against actual operations and cost centers.

rubrics_metrics.name: PWS content definition (technical/functional/performance characteristics)
rubrics_metrics.description: A Performance Work Statement is a statement of the technical, functional and performance characteristics of the work to be performed; identifies essential functions; determines performance factors including location, units of work, quantity of units, and the quality and timeliness of the work units. It serves as the scope of the work and the basis for all costs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this definition as a checklist when drafting the PWS: include technical specs, essential functions, performance factors (locations, units, quantities), quality metrics, and timeliness metrics. Link each performance requirement to cost elements.

rubrics_metrics.name: PWS preparation team composition and competence
rubrics_metrics.description: Preparing the PWS requires putting a team of military and civil service employees together to capture the specific requirements of commercial activity in writing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Select and train PWS writing teams in legal/requirements writing; include functional experts, cost estimators, and contracting specialists to avoid poorly written criteria that could expose the Government to poor performance, legal action, or cost increases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Risk of misrepresentation and contracting officer oversight
rubrics_metrics.description: There is the potential for misrepresentation on the part of A-76 team members in an effort to keep their jobs. Oversight by the Contracting Officer during development of the acquisition strategy is the primary place one would expect to catch discrepancies in the PWS.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Institute independent oversight and review checkpoints (Contracting Officer and others) during acquisition strategy and PWS development to detect and correct errors or biased representations. Maintain audit trails and approvals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Legal statutory restrictions on outsourcing specific services
rubrics_metrics.description: Specific legal restrictions include the prohibition against outsourcing fire fighting and policing services aboard installations, and congressional mandates that a given percentage of work in depot maintenance facilities be performed by Government employees; prior Defense Authorization Acts have placed restrictions on competitive sourcing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check applicable statutes and Defense Authorization/appropriations language before proposing studies or solicitations. Maintain a list of prohibited or restricted functions and ensure compliance in nominations and solicitations.
